sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: An erect annual herb commonly around 2 m tall, with palmately lobed leaves and large yellow or whitish flowers with a dark purple centre. Its long, ribbed capsules contain many round seeds. It is widely cultivated in tropical and warm-temperate regions; its exact wild origin remains uncertain.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The immature capsules are widely eaten as a vegetable. Kew also records animal-food and medicinal uses; the sources consulted do not establish specific toxicity details.
